## Incident Report — Traffic Analysis Exercise 2022-01-07

**Evidence:** `2022-01-07-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap` (5,880 packets, SHA256 `a86b11ee443ee59d95e4590bdf761235c5d240128d6d195233d065ab57777e8b`). No IDS/Suricata alert exports were present in the evidence directory — findings below are derived directly from packet analysis with tshark.

### Victim host
| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 | 192.168.1.216 |
| MAC address | 9c:5c:8e:32:58:f9 (ASUS network adapter) |
| Windows hostname | DESKTOP-GXMYNO2 (confirmed via DHCP request, mDNS, LLMNR, NBNS) |
| Domain | spoonwatch.net (DC: SPOONWATCH-DC, 192.168.1.2) |
| Logged-in user | **steve.smith** (confirmed via Kerberos AS-REQ/TGS-REQ CNameString exchanges between 192.168.1.216 and the DC) |

### Malware family
**Vidar Stealer — behaviorally attributed, not signature-confirmed** (no IDS/AV output exists in this evidence set to give a signature match). The attribution rests on a well-documented Vidar TTP fingerprint observed directly in the capture:

1. The infected host makes six sequential HTTP GETs to a numbered image path (`/osk//1.jpg` through `/osk//7.jpg`, skipping none but out of numeric order) which return **PE32/PE32+ binaries mislabeled as `image/jpeg`**, not actual images.
2. Those six binaries are the exact set of legitimate Mozilla NSS/Thunderbird redistributable DLLs Vidar is known to fetch to decrypt browser-stored credentials: `freebl3.dll`, `mozglue.dll`, `msvcp140.dll` (renamed), `nss3.dll`, `softokn3.dll`, and `vcruntime140.dll` (renamed) — identified via embedded PDB paths (e.g. `...obj-thunderbird\security\nss3.pdb`, `...obj-thunderbird\mozglue\build\mozglue.pdb`, `...obj-thunderbird\security\nss\lib\softoken\softoken_softokn3\softokn3.pdb`).
3. A follow-up POST to `/osk//main.php` (empty 200 response) acts as a check-in/ack.
4. The host then **uploads** a 379,629-byte multipart POST to `/osk/` containing a file named `_5861695120.zip`, whose internal structure (`autofill/Google Chrome_Default.txt`, `autofill/Microsoft Edge_Default.txt`, `cc/Google Chrome_Default.txt`, `cc/Microsoft Edge_Default.txt`, `cookies/Google Chrome_Network.txt`) is the characteristic **Vidar stealer log layout** (per-browser autofill / credit-card / cookie exfiltration folders).

All other external traffic from the host (Bing, MSN, Windows Update, Microsoft telemetry/WNS/delivery-optimization domains over TLS with legitimate SNI) is benign background Windows/OS noise and not part of the infection chain.

### Indicators of Compromise

**Command-and-control**
- C2 endpoint: **2.56.57.108:80** (plain HTTP, single TCP stream #65, no DNS lookup preceded it — IP is hardcoded in the malware)
- No malicious domain observed — the malware talks to the C2 by raw IP only.

**Malicious URLs (all http://2.56.57.108)**
- `http://2.56.57.108/osk//1.jpg`
- `http://2.56.57.108/osk//2.jpg`
- `http://2.56.57.108/osk//3.jpg`
- `http://2.56.57.108/osk//4.jpg`
- `http://2.56.57.108/osk//5.jpg`
- `http://2.56.57.108/osk//6.jpg`
- `http://2.56.57.108/osk//7.jpg`
- `http://2.56.57.108/osk//main.php`
- `http://2.56.57.108/osk/` (exfil upload endpoint)

**Transferred files (downloaded, disguised as .jpg, actually PE binaries) and SHA256**
| Delivered as | Actual type | SHA256 |
|---|---|---|
| 1.jpg | PE32 DLL (console) | `16574f51785b0e2fc29c2c61477eb47bb39f714829999511dc8952b43ab17660` |
| 2.jpg | PE32 DLL (GUI) — freebl3.dll | `a770ecba3b08bbabd0a567fc978e50615f8b346709f8eb3cfacf3faab24090ba` |
| 3.jpg | PE32 DLL (GUI) — mozglue.dll | `3fe6b1c54b8cf28f571e0c5d6636b4069a8ab00b4f11dd842cfec00691d0c9cd` |
| 4.jpg | PE32 DLL (console) — msvcp140.dll | `334e69ac9367f708ce601a6f490ff227d6c20636da5222f148b25831d22e13d4` |
| 5.jpg | PE32 DLL (GUI) — nss3.dll | `e2935b5b28550d47dc971f456d6961f20d1633b4892998750140e0eaa9ae9d78` |
| 6.jpg | PE32 DLL (GUI) — softokn3.dll | `43536adef2ddcc811c28d35fa6ce3031029a2424ad393989db36169ff2995083` |
| 7.jpg | PE32 DLL (console) — vcruntime140.dll | `c40bb03199a2054dabfc7a8e01d6098e91de7193619effbd0f142a7bf031c14d` |

**Exfiltrated file**
- `_5861695120.zip` (379,629 bytes) — uploaded via POST to `/osk/`; contains stolen browser autofill, saved credit-card, and cookie data from Google Chrome and Microsoft Edge.

### Note on other .cab/.exe downloads
`am_delta_patch_1.355.1569.0_...exe` and the `35969515/35969516/35969632*.cab` files were retrieved from `download.windowsupdate.com` / `au.download.windowsupdate.com` (23.38.189.201/225) — these are legitimate Windows Defender/Update Delivery Optimization files, not part of the compromise.
